items.message:
High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible Around high tide 
We are entering a sequence of Spring tides that may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible around 06:45 on Friday 11th September. Flooding is forecast to affect locations at Porlock Bay, with low lying land and roads expected to be most affected, particularly around the coastline between Gore Point and Hurlstone Point including Porlock Weir. The first high tide is at 06:45 on Friday with a peak height of 6.12m and a F4 north westerly wind. The second high tide is at 19:00 on Friday with a peak height of 6.37m and a F4 westerly wind 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 12:19PM on 10 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

High tides overnight may lead to flooding. 
Although the midday tide today Friday 11 September, is expected to peak just below the Flood Alert threshold, the following tide is forecast to exceed this.
Flooding is possible from 10:30 PM tonight Friday 11 September to 02:30 AM on Saturday 12 September, peaking at 00:30 AM.
Areas most at risk lie within the Sandside area of North Morecambe Bay. Locations most affected will be coastal roads and footpaths. 
We are closely monitoring the situation. 
Avoid beaches and coastal promenades, which may be flooded . Do not drive through flood water or put yourself or others at risk. 
This message will be updated by 05:00PM today Friday 11 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.description: Wyre estuary from Fleetwood and Knott End to Little Eccleston
items.message: A flood alert remains in place for tonight's high tide at Hambleton which will peak at 00:45am on 12/09/2026. This flood alert is forecast to remain in place for the following three high tides until Sunday.  This lunchtime's tide (Friday) peaking at 12:30 PM is not forecast to reach the alert threshold.

items.description: The Essex coast from Clacton to and including, St Peters Flat and the Colne and Blackwater estuaries
items.message:
High tides today may lead to flooding. 
Flooding is possible between 11:45am and 1:45pm today, Friday 11th September. 
Clacton Promenade, Lee-over-Sands and Brightlingsea sea front may see some wave overtopping and spray. The Strood at Mersea Island, Coast Road and car parks on the front at West Mersea, and the Hythe and Promenade at Maldon may be flooded. The detailed forecast is for a peak level at Clacton of 2.72mAODN at 12:45pm, on Friday 11th September, which is 0.27m above tide tables, wind force 3, north westerly. Tides are expected to be higher than usual, due to the forecast weather conditions during spring tides. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded . 
This message will be updated by 5:00PM on 11 September 2026 or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. 
We do not expect to see similar impacts from the next high tide.   
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.   
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger. Never drive through flood water,  just 30cm of fast flowing water is enough to move your car.
